ranking.note: Raised to P2: instructions that are actively wrong and leave users running stale multiprocess helper binaries are the top docs failure mode, above clarifying/consolidating docs
Moved up: it corrects overstated privacy guarantees and labels the feature experimental in a branch that will actually ship (31.2), not just routine backport bookkeeping
Moved up: corrects a privacy-relevant inaccuracy (transient vs persistent I2P identity, wallet txs not covered) which outranks consolidation and internal-doc work
Moved down: internal code-comment documentation for contributors ranks below docs that correct or supply information users and integrators act on
Lowered to P4: purely informational BIP-listing and release-note sync on a maintenance branch, with none of the misleading-claim correction that justifies the 31.x backport

inconsistencies: #35480 and #35518 both address open issue #14278 (notification semantics for external integrators) from different angles (ZMQ topics vs -*notify shell hooks); review #35518 first since it establishes the general asynchronous/no-ordering contract that #35480 then specializes for ZMQ.

#35858 (new doc/privacy.md, moves content out of doc/i2p.md and doc/tor.md) and #36348 (edits doc/i2p.md about -privatebroadcast) touch the same text about private broadcast scope; order matters — merge the small correction #36348 first, or fold its wording into #35858, otherwise the correction is lost or conflicts when content is relocated.
#36319 (31.x) and #36401 (30.x) both backport #36377 (BIP 461 in bips.md); they are parallel branch copies of work already merged in master, so verifying the master parents once covers both.

#36319 and #36348 both adjust how -privatebroadcast privacy is described; the 31.x backport ships the 'experimental / risk reduction' framing to users, while #36348 refines the same feature's docs in master — keep the wording aligned between them.
result.notes: This list is mostly mid-weight docs work; only one PR (#36441) is a genuine 'documentation tells the user to do the wrong thing' case and only one (#36101) carries leverage over other open PRs, so the band spread is deliberately narrow at the top and the P3 ordering is driven by whether the text misleads (privacy/notification semantics) versus merely consolidates.
